speaker: The Minister of State for Home Affairs (Mr Desmond Tan) (for the Minister for Home Affairs)
text: This is not surprising, given that this group is more likely to be searching for jobs and are also more willing to try out online or remote work.

speaker: The Minister of State for Home Affairs (Mr Desmond Tan) (for the Minister for Home Affairs)
text: Job scams exploit victims' interest in easy, work-from-home settings, such as to generate hype on e-commerce platforms, or traction for social media accounts and content.

speaker: The Minister of State for Home Affairs (Mr Desmond Tan) (for the Minister for Home Affairs)
text: In many of these cases, scammers had created professional-looking apps with references to e-commerce listings or social media posts, to enhance the appearance of legitimacy.

speaker: The Minister of State for Home Affairs (Mr Desmond Tan) (for the Minister for Home Affairs)
text: In this way, the scammers deceive the victims into thinking that they were participating in a genuine job scheme.

speaker: The Minister of State for Home Affairs (Mr Desmond Tan) (for the Minister for Home Affairs)
text: Scammers would then require the victims to download apps and set up user accounts by transferring funds to bank accounts that are created by the scammers.

speaker: The Minister of State for Home Affairs (Mr Desmond Tan) (for the Minister for Home Affairs)
text: Victims were then instructed to perform tasks, such as purchasing of items or clicking on posts to generate views, before they could receive their commissions.

speaker: The Minister of State for Home Affairs (Mr Desmond Tan) (for the Minister for Home Affairs)
text: Victims usually only realised that they were scammed when they did not receive their commissions or were unable to withdraw money from their accounts after performing their assigned tasks.

speaker: The Minister of State for Home Affairs (Mr Desmond Tan) (for the Minister for Home Affairs)
text: To address this, education is key to protect people from falling prey to scams.

speaker: The Minister of State for Home Affairs (Mr Desmond Tan) (for the Minister for Home Affairs)
text: Our anti-scam public education campaign, called "Spot the Signs.

speaker: The Minister of State for Home Affairs (Mr Desmond Tan) (for the Minister for Home Affairs)
text: Stop the Crimes." is in its second year and its coverage includes job scams.

speaker: The Minister of State for Home Affairs (Mr Desmond Tan) (for the Minister for Home Affairs)
text: The Police regularly share crime information, including scam prevention advice, with the community and grassroots volunteers, for the purpose of their engagement with residents about scams.

speaker: The Minister of State for Home Affairs (Mr Desmond Tan) (for the Minister for Home Affairs)
text: Volunteer Crime Prevention Ambassadors from the National Crime Prevention Council also share crime prevention tips with residents during their engagements.

speaker: The Minister of State for Home Affairs (Mr Desmond Tan) (for the Minister for Home Affairs)
text: Besides education, we have also stepped up enforcement efforts.

speaker: The Minister of State for Home Affairs (Mr Desmond Tan) (for the Minister for Home Affairs)
text: Specialised units have been set up in SPF to disrupt scammers' operations and these include the Anti-Scam Division (ASD).

speaker: The Minister of State for Home Affairs (Mr Desmond Tan) (for the Minister for Home Affairs)
text: Specifically for job scams, SPF has conducted targeted operations to dismantle the syndicates.

speaker: The Minister of State for Home Affairs (Mr Desmond Tan) (for the Minister for Home Affairs)
text: Given the transnational nature of job scams, the Police have stepped up collaboration with foreign law enforcement agencies.

speaker: The Minister of State for Home Affairs (Mr Desmond Tan) (for the Minister for Home Affairs)
text: As I had mentioned, the best defence against scams is a discerning public.

speaker: The Minister of State for Home Affairs (Mr Desmond Tan) (for the Minister for Home Affairs)
text: When looking for jobs, members of the public should always exercise healthy scepticism and verify the legitimacy of the job offer.

speaker: The Minister of State for Home Affairs (Mr Desmond Tan) (for the Minister for Home Affairs)
text: They should also refrain from making any advance payments to secure a job.

speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
text: Will the Ministry consider working with Workforce Singapore and NTUC's e2i to include measures for job scams in their job coaching curriculum for senior jobseekers?

speaker: Mr Desmond Tan
text: Indeed, IMDA constantly work with the stakeholders and agencies to expand our outreach to different stakeholders, to different target groups and to help prevent scams from happening.

speaker: Mr Desmond Tan
text: We will take into consideration the Member's suggestions in our continued engagement and education efforts to prevent scams from reaching especially our seniors.
